title: Beyond the 956: Tom Jackson, Broncos 'Orange Crush' star and ESPN legend, dies at 75
excerpt: Tom Jackson, the Denver Broncos linebacker who anchored the 'Orange Crush' defense and spent nearly three decades on ESPN's Sunday NFL Countdown, died Friday, November 20, 2026, at 75. His family informed ESPN, and the news was announced Sunday by his longtime on-air partner Chris Berman.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Tom Jackson, the Denver Broncos linebacker who anchored the legendary “Orange Crush” defense and then became one of the most familiar voices in American sports television, has died at 75.

Jackson died Friday, November 20, 2026. No cause of death has been released. His family informed ESPN of his death, and at the family’s wishes the news was not announced until Sunday morning, when his longtime on-air partner Chris Berman shared it at the start of ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown.

A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson played 14 seasons for the Broncos, from 1973 to 1986, starting 177 games. He was the inspirational leader of Denver’s first Super Bowl team in 1977 and a cornerstone of the “Orange Crush” defense. He was a three-time Pro Bowler and a two-time Associated Press All-Pro, recording 20 interceptions in 191 career games, three of them returned for touchdowns. He was inducted into the Broncos’ Ring of Fame in 1992.

After retiring, Jackson joined ESPN in 1987 as the network’s first NFL analyst and spent nearly three decades alongside Berman on Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime, becoming a fixture of football Sundays for generations of fans. He retired from ESPN in 2016 and briefly returned in 2019. In 2015, he received the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame, and ESPN’s studio in Bristol, Connecticut, is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio.

“The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history,” the Broncos said in a statement.

Berman called Jackson his best friend professionally and personally. “There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him,” Berman said on Sunday’s show.

Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and daughters Taylor and Morgan.

Sources: The Associated Press; Reuters; ESPN; Denver Broncos.
